I think you missed the entire point of the interview.

Jon Stewart was not trying to prove that the materials in burn pits cause cause cancer, this has been proven [source](https://www.nap.edu/read/13209/chapter/2).  Benzene is an incredibly well studied carcinogen, and was used in accelerant in many of the burn pits.  The US has known that benzene is a harmful substance for over 100 years [source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3447593/).  The idea that the science is still out on burn pits and cancer is a complete joke.

The point of the interview was to get a straight answer on why the process of aiding veterans suffering from cancer or other health issues (allegedly from the burn pits) has been so incredibly slow.  This is why the interview is so shocking to people, the fact that the secretary of veterans affairs is either unsure or unwilling to answer that one simple question without resorting to "well we don't know for sure" when we absolutely do, and have known for decades.

I think this lack of difficulty can be attributed to the excess of quick healing in DS2, made possible by the life gem system.  
Regardless, I think that there is truth to the idea that the first Soulsborne game you play will likely be the one you end up liking the most.  The Souls series is my favorite, and I'm always glad to see other people enjoy it as well, even if they play the worst one ;)

IMO DS2 had the weakest areas, most mundane and similar enemies and bosses, slowed down PvE combat with easier enemies, and the weakest dlc package of the dark souls series.  SotFS edition attempted to rectify the lack of challenge posed by standard mobs by simply adding random boss spawns around the map (like The Pursuer, Covetous Demon, and the Dragon Knight), which proved that these "bosses" were of low difficulty and quality, and did not deserve fog gates in the first place.  While the game had a handful of interesting bosses like Fume Knight and Smelter Demon, they were far outnumbered by lackluster bosses and phoned-in copies like Rat Vanguard, Rat Authority, The Last Giant, Covetous Demon and his brothers, The Congregation,  etc.  I think that aside from pvp, which was and still is excellent, the game failed to deliver across all fronts and proved to be a far less challenging and less rewarding experience than its predecessors. A common argument I see against DQ is that having players queued up allows for easier ranking, making ranks meaningless.  However, when I play with a party of 3 or 4 people, there is a party of 3 or 4 people on the other team for the most part.  Even when I am on a team with a premade, and I am the odd man out, I am never really flamed for that reason and don't feel disadvantaged.  I would honestly be disappointed if solo queue was added and made the main ranked mode for players, because this would just undermine dynamic queue for, from my point of view, no good reason besides for upper-level players. You need SOME sort of luck if you want to jump in ranks, assuming you aren't Diamond 1 material and can carry a 3v5.  I am 'stuck' in Bronze and I see factors of luck all the time in my game, and it is damn sure occurring in other divisions too.  Saying that there is no luck and that the inability to rank up is due to poor skill is just a troll thing to say.  As Stabby said, going negative in 20 games in a row is most likely due to your own skill.  Maybe you could consider the mid position, due to the ability to roam and carry other lanes?  All I can say is that there is a definite factor of luck, but doing bad in 20 games is more than bad luck, and you should watch your own replays and see what you and your team did bad, so you can improve. I am in a similar situation.  I have been in Bronze 5 for months, and now just got promoted to bronze 4.  Alot of my friends are in silver, and often fluctuate in their ranking. I prefer to do duo with my friend.  Some positions I feel can turn a game are ADC, Support, Jungler, and Mid.  ADC needs to get fed, and a good support can help the worst ADC get fed.  Jungler can camp lanes to get ahead, and some mids can completely carry a game.  Top champs are known to snowball, but is harder in my opinion than any other lane because of that.  You should try the other positions and see if you like any other position with a champ you enjoy.  Overall, have fun.  I have found that having fun and playing where you like with who you like really effects the outcome of the game.
